summary:
[  edit  ]
The Basis  SOP  provides a set of operations applicable to the parametric space of spline curves and surfaces. The parametric space, also known as the "domain" of a NURBS or Bzier primitive, is defined by one basis in the U direction and, if the primitive is a surface, another basis in the V direction. The size of the domain is given by the values of the knots that make up the basis.
The Basis  SOP  contains both ratio-preserving and non ratio-preserving operations.
If the basis reparameterization does not change the distance ratios between knots, the shape of a NURBS primitive is not affected. If the ratios are not preserved, however, a NURBS primitive will change shape in the area influenced by the modified knots; furthermore, if the primitive is a NURBS or Bzier surface, any profiles it may contain will be affected as well.
For more information about bases and knots see Breakpoints, Knots, and Spline Basis in the  Primitive  and  Spline  articles.

parameters.label: Group
parameters.name: group
parameters.description: Group  of spline primitives (accepts patterns, as described in: Scripting Guide). Non-spline types are ignored.

parameters.label: Edit the U Basis
parameters.name: ubasis
parameters.description: Enable editing of the U Basis.

parameters.label: Parameterization
parameters.name: uparmtype
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select the method of parameterization in u from the options below.

parameters.label: Unchanged
parameters.name: nochange
parameters.description: Does not change the basis.

parameters.label: Uniform
parameters.name: uniform
parameters.description: Distributes all the knots evenly, maintaining the basis origin and length. Recommended only for regular shapes.

parameters.label: Chord Length
parameters.name: chord
parameters.description: Computes the knot ratios based on the distances between successive CVs. This is the most common and most effective parameterization method.

parameters.label: Centripetal
parameters.name: centripetal
parameters.description: Similar to the chord length method. Recommended for shapes containing sharp turns.

parameters.label: Manual: Single
parameters.name: manualone
parameters.description: Loads the basis with the knots listed in the "Knot Sequence" below. If the  SOP  input contains several primitives, only the basis of the first spline primitive will be affected.

parameters.label: Manual: Propagated
parameters.name: manualall
parameters.description: Same as above + it copies the basis to the basis of all the other spline primitives in the model or in the group. Using this feature on curves that have the point count and degree will generate cleaner surfaces, i.e. surfaces with fewer isoparms.

parameters.label: Knotslide
parameters.name: slide
parameters.description: Shift clusters of knots within the basis. See  Knotslide  (From  Paramaterization Menu ) for discussion.

parameters.label: Knot Sequence
parameters.name: uknots
parameters.description: The basis of the first spline primitive in the input loads its knot sequence with the data specified in this field when the  Parameterization  is set to  Manual . The values must be in ascending order, and their total count must match the number of knots in the basis. To ensure an exact count, click on the  Read Basis  button to read the original knot sequence into this field.

parameters.label: Read Basis
parameters.name: uread
parameters.description: Loads the original knots of the basis into the  Knot Sequence  field when the  Parameterization  type is  Manual .

parameters.label: Range
parameters.name: urange
parameters.description: ⊞  - Range specifies the domain interval to be shifted. All the knots captured in this range are shifted by the same amount as far as the closest neighbouring knot on either side.

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.name: ubias
parameters.description: Bias indicates the direction and the amount of translation. A  Bias  of 0.5 does not displace the knots at all. As the  Bias  decreases, the knot cluster migrates closer to its left-neighbouring knot. A  Bias  greater than 0.5 forces a migration to the right.

parameters.label: Concatenate
parameters.name: uconcat
parameters.description: Indicates whether the bases of the input spline primitives should be concatenated such that the last knot of the first primitive coincides with the first knot of the second primitive, and so on. This operation is performed before the ones below it, thus allowing a whole set of bases to be mapped onto a given interval (usually [0,1]) while enforcing basis continuity.

parameters.label: Origin
parameters.name: udoorigin
parameters.description: Enables the Origin parameter.

parameters.label: Origin
parameters.name: uorigin
parameters.description: The new origin of the basis, or the origin of the cummulated bases if  Concatenation  is  On .

parameters.label: Length
parameters.name: udolength
parameters.description: Enables the Length parameter.

parameters.label: Length
parameters.name: ulength
parameters.description: The new length of the basis, or the total length of the cummulated bases if  Concatenation  is  On . The  Length , which represents the distance between the first and last knot, must be greater than zero.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.name: udoscale
parameters.description: Enables the Scale parameter.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.name: uscale
parameters.description: The multiplier applied to the basis starting at the basis origin. The  Scale  must be greater than zero.

parameters.label: Raise to
parameters.name: uraise
parameters.description: Enables the Raise to parameter.

parameters.label: Raise U to
parameters.name: orderu
parameters.description: The only operation here is raising the order (or degree) of the spline basis. Valid orders range from 2 to 11. Orders lower than the current spline order are ignored. The operation preserves the shape of the primitive.

parameters.label: Production Tip:  Before applying a spline
parameters.description: based texture projection with the Texture  SOP , remap the U and/or V bases of the spline surface between 0 and 1 to ensure a complete mapping of the texture. If a single texture map must be shared by several surfaces, the surface bases should be concatenated prior to being remapped.

parameters.label: num_points
parameters.description: Number of points in this  SOP .

parameters.label: last_vbo_update_time
parameters.description: Time spent in another thread updating geometry data on the  GPU  from the  SOP 's CPU data. As it is part of another thread, this time is not part of the usual frame time.

parameters.label: last_meta_vbo_update_time
parameters.description: Time spent in another thread updating meta surface geometry data (such as metaballs or nurbs) on the  GPU  from the  SOP 's CPU data. As it is part of another thread, this time is not part of the usual frame time.

parameters.description: Number of times the operator has cooked since the process started.

parameters.label: cook_abs_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the absolute time.

parameters.label: cook_start_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator started cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cook_end_time

Import Select POP * **¿Qué hace?** Este operador es fundamental para **cargar geometrías de archivos externos** o de otros componentes de TouchDesigner como USD COMP y FBX COMP. Es una puerta de entrada para traer modelos 3D y otros tipos de geometría a tu entorno POP. * **Características clave:** * Puede cargar varios tipos de geometría soportados por USD COMP o FBX COMP, como **Mallas (`Mesh`), Puntos (`Points`), Curvas o Patches NURBS, Curvas de Base (`Basis Curves`)**. * Cada geometría importada puede ser una primitiva única o un conjunto de primitivas fusionadas para un mejor rendimiento. * Si los tipos de geometría no son compatibles directamente con POPs, se **convierten automáticamente a triángulos, quads, line strips y primitivas de punto**. * Cuando se fusionan geometrías, se crea un operador `Info DAT` junto a este POP, que muestra las rutas originales de las primitivas dentro del archivo importado. * Tiene sus *
